C6.1: Brighten a bass or lead at the source, so it gains bite and edge while the note you play stays exactly where it was.
C6.2: A lead that tears and seems to speak like a vowel, swept by one knob you can ride through a build.
C6.3: Thin, nasal pulse basses and slowly shifting tones come from here, giving a held note life without any filter movement.
C6.4: Growling basses, glassy bells and bright strikes that mellow all come from one oscillator shaking another, and you choose how fierce it gets.
C6.5: Metallic, clanging tones for hits and strange textures are yours once you can predict what two multiplied oscillators will give.
C6.C: Hearing a gritty sound in a track and knowing whether it was bent, torn, shaken or multiplied means you can rebuild it yourself.
C7.1: Add grit and weight to a clean bass, choosing between a gentle bend and a harsh buzz, then blend the clean sound back underneath.
C7.2: Carve out a muddy patch or lift the part of a sound that helps it cut through, once you have found it by sweeping.
C7.3: Keep a bass line steady in level from note to note while still letting the punch at the front of each note through.
C7.4: Turn a thin, narrow sound into a wide, thick pad or lead, and know when to reach for this over stacked voices.
C7.5: Echoes that land on the beat become part of your rhythm, filling the gaps after a stab or lead with repeats.
C7.6: Place a sound close up or far away in a space of any size, without the tail smearing a fast line.
C7.C: When a sound in your track feels wrong, you will hear whether the tone, the repeats or the space needs fixing and go straight there.
